uncited: It builds on [Importance Sampling for Sphere Surface Area](2223-importance-sampling-for-sphere-surface-area.md) by adding spatial variation and occlusion awareness via the NGP, distinguishing it from static [Importance Sampling](9521-importance-sampling.md) strategies.
- A pre-trained NGP mapping $\mathbf{x}$ to scalar parameters.
- A set of $M$ sample directions $\{\boldsymbol{\omega}^j_{in}\}_{j=1}^M$ generated by a proposal distribution $p$.
- Incident radiance estimates $\hat{L}_{NeRF}(\mathbf{x}, \boldsymbol{\omega}^j_{in})$ from a NeRF cache or similar estimator.
- A mixture of $L$ vMF distributions parameterized by $\{\lambda_\ell(\mathbf{x}), \boldsymbol{\mu}_\ell(\mathbf{x}), \kappa_\ell(\mathbf{x})\}_{\ell=1}^L$.
- The probability density value $\text{mixture}(\mathbf{d}; \mathbf{x})$ for any direction $\mathbf{d}$.
**Output:** The MLP predicts $5L$ scalars for each point $\mathbf{x}$.
- **Time Complexity:** Depends on the number of lobes $L$ and the NGP lookup cost.
For $L=128$, the mixture evaluation involves 128 vMF PDF computations and a sum.
NGP lookup is $O(1)$ with hash collisions.
Performance depends on the quality of the NeRF cache for radiance estimation.
It is part of a broader approach to inverse rendering that uses neural representations (NGPs) to accelerate radiance cache computations and importance sampling.
The use of vMF mixtures for directional distributions is a common technique in physically-based rendering, adapted here for spatial variation and occlusion awareness.
